_comment: Single source of truth for the MCP tools this server registers -- issue #85.
Before this file there were four hand-synced copies of the tool list (the register*Tool
installer/verify-dxt.mjs), and the test that claimed to catch drift between them compared
the manifest against its own local literal instead. See docs/adr/0015.
JSON rather than TypeScript so the installer's plain-Node scripts can read it directly,
with no build step and no dependency on server/dist -- which is gitignored, so requiring
it would mean `npm run test:installer` failed on a fresh clone.
bundleDescription is the one-line blurb shown in the .mcpb bundle's manifest, NOT the
tool's real MCP description (those are long, Claude-facing, and live at each register*Tool
Adding a tool: add it here and register it in server/src/. Three tests then prove the
three consumers agree -- toolNames.test.ts (what the server really registers),
installer/dxt/manifest.test.mjs (what the manifest declares), and installer/verify-dxt.mjs
(what a packed .mcpb actually serves over stdio).

tools.name: run_lua
tools.bundleDescription: Run a freshly-authored Lua script against the open FH project via the Bridge plugin.

tools.name: describe_project
tools.bundleDescription: Fixed, built-in census of the open FH project (record counts, flag/tag breakdowns).

tools.name: author_fh_plugin
tools.bundleDescription: Scaffold a standalone FH Report/Query plugin for the user to save and install.

tools.name: install_fh_plugin
tools.bundleDescription: Write a plugin author_fh_plugin generated into FH's own Plugins folder.

tools.name: grep_fh_help
tools.bundleDescription: Full-text search over FH's own help corpus.

tools.name: check_fh_help_updates
tools.bundleDescription: Check for and pull down updated FH help content.

tools.name: search_gedcom_knowledge
tools.bundleDescription: Search the GEDCOM/FH domain-knowledge corpus (FTF, Shared Facts, Source Templates, ...).
